curriculum.resolved: Foundational two-digit place-value refresher; no syllabus certification or full-grade coverage

objectives.text: Explain a digit’s value in a two-digit number by counting its tens or ones.

concept.hook: How can a single digit tell us about a whole group of cubes?
concept.analogy: Actual cube quantities become rods of ten; each rod keeps ten visible parts.
concept.arc: Count ten ones, bundle a ten, build twenty three, connect each digit to its units, then reason about four in forty two.

scenes.title: Can ten cubes become one group?
scenes.narration: Let's count these cubes. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Join all ten cubes into one rod. Every cube is still here. We have only grouped them. This is one ten, worth ten ones.

visual.label: Ten individual cubes make one group of ten

scenes.title: Build twenty three
scenes.narration: Here are twenty three single cubes. Bundle them into groups of ten. Our first group makes one ten. Our second group makes another ten. Three cubes are left over. Two tens and three ones: we write twenty three.

visual.label: Two groups of ten and three leftover ones

cues.phrase: Here are twenty three single cubes
Bundle them into groups of ten

scenes.title: What does the two tell us?
scenes.narration: Look at our twenty three: two tens and three ones. Focus on the tens. One rod is ten. Two rods are twenty. The digit two counts the rods, not single cubes. Read the value: two tens are worth twenty.

visual.label: The digit two counts two tens, worth twenty

scenes.title: Same number, different units
scenes.narration: Our number is still twenty three. Focus on the three ones. Each loose cube is worth one. Count them: one, two, three. Read the value: three ones are worth three. Two counts tens here; three counts ones. The place tells us which units to count.

visual.label: The digit three counts three ones, worth three

cues.phrase: Our number is still twenty three

scenes.title: Your turn: look at the place
scenes.narration: In forty two, what is the value of the digit four? Think about which place it is in, and what each group is worth.

items: In 42, what is the value of the digit 4?
visual.label: Find the value of the selected digit

scenes.title: Let’s check with blocks
scenes.narration: Here is forty two: four tens and two ones. Focus on the four tens. Count their value: ten, twenty, thirty, forty. Each rod holds ten cubes. Read the answer: four tens are forty. So the digit four is worth forty, not four ones.

scenes.title: Find the place. Count its value.
scenes.narration: Come back to twenty three. Focus on the tens again. The two counts two groups of ten, worth twenty. Read the whole number: twenty and three make twenty three. To find a digit's value, find its place and count what those groups are worth.

visual.label: Place tells us the units; the digit counts those units
